what: How long each crystal's phonon modes ring, as a quality factor Q = line position / line width (both in cm^-1), from the Raman line width at room temperature. Q has no units, so it survives the transposition from terahertz to audio unchanged: a mode rings for about Q/pi cycles before falling to 1/e, whatever pitch it is played at. In seconds: tau = Q / (pi * f).
how_used: One anchor Q per crystal, taken from its strongest Raman line, is given to every mode of that crystal (so higher modes die faster in seconds simply because they are higher). Where a mode is known to be different, it gets its own Q (the quartz soft mode).
honesty: Only the rows marked 'measured' come from a source I found this cycle. 'estimated' rows are my reading of typical room-temperature Raman widths for that mineral and need checking against a paper before anyone calls them physics. 'placeholder' rows are the two hypothesis lattices, which have no mineral behind them.

crystals.name: Diamond
crystals.source: first-order Raman line of diamond, 'typical FWHM 1.65 +/- 0.02 cm^-1 at room temperature' as quoted from Prawer & Nemanich, 'Raman spectroscopy of diamond and doped diamond' (Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A, 2004; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8233307). Other sources give 1-1.5 cm^-1, which would ring longer still.

crystals.name: Fluorite
crystals.source: CaF2 T2g line at 323 cm^-1 with FWHM 12 cm^-1 for a pure CaF2 standard (Caries Research 27(6):445, https://karger.com/cre/article/27/6/445/84242). That was a powder standard measured for a dental study; a clear single crystal is likely narrower, so fluorite may ring longer than this.

crystals.name: Ruby
crystals.source: corundum A1g line at 418 cm^-1, its strongest; width estimated. The sapphire temperature study (Appl. Opt. 56, 8598 (2017), https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1406891) measures it but I could not read the room-temperature number out of the PDF this cycle.

crystals.name: Amethyst
crystals.source: alpha-quartz A1 line at 464 cm^-1, FWHM 7-8 cm^-1 at 300 K, from the quartz pressure-sensor study (Am. Mineral. 85, 1725 (2000), https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/msa/ammin/article-abstract/85/11-12/1725/133600) as summarised by a search; I did not read the paper itself

exceptions.source: the soft mode that drives quartz's alpha-beta transition is known to be broad and to broaden fast with temperature; width estimated
